Messages.Author: Orpheus
Messages.Body:
Hello all,

I have been assured that some group 4 Camarilla vampires will come out in
the Anarchs.
Whether this is true or not isn't the point here (I'm not a playtester so
can't be sure ; if I was I wouldn't speak about it yet). If you want to
discuss it start a new thread. A few Group 4 Camarilla vampires isn't
dramatical, it's just useless (they just re-released group 2 Cammies, and
now you can't mix them anymore with the enw vampires ?!). But it needs to
STOP NOW !!!
The reason why I'm launching this now and not waiting for Anarchs is that I
guess game conception needs time, and that by then the new extension will
already be thought over. So I'm launching an ultimatum and a petition HERE
and NOW :

I, Orpheus, Prince of Marseille, France, hereby declare that if any
GROUP 5 vampire, or any Sabbatic (or Bloodlines) GROUP 4 vampire ever comes
out, I will :

- stop buying new products
- resign from my Princeship

I ask EVERYBODY who shares these feelings to add a "me too" to this thread.
If White Wolf sees that a product designed to "force us to buy" has the
opposite effect, I think and hope that they will stop the insanity NOW. Up
until now they have heeded our thoughts and needs, more or less, so we have
to show them what we want, or rather what we DON'T WANT !!!

I must say that I still love this game (just wait to see my new site...), am
still motivated to continue my job of promoting it, and for now will still
encourage people to buy new extensions. But I also know what will the
difference in sales will be the day when I won't. Or, for that matter, the
day when any of my players will see Group 5 Cammies or Group 4 Sabbat.

It's up to us, guys, let's show the businessmen what we want.

Sincerely yours, and more than a little pissed off,
--
Orpheus

http://cypheranima.free.fr
http://no.exit.free.fr
news://news.zoo-logique.org/VTES-francophone

"After all, what is an angel but a demon yet to fall ?"
(Nancy A. Collins)

Look, if you don't believe in grouping, you don't believe in
grouping, but I'm not sure that boycott threats are going to
change any decisionmakers' minds at White Wolf.

The grouping rule is supposed to keep the playing field level for
newer players who will never have access to group 1 vampires. In
the future, they might also not have access to group 2, 3, etc
vampires. The grouping rule guarantees that they'll always have
access to a comparable pool of most-recently-printed vampires as
the one that longtime players have access to.

It also is supposed to keep "perfect crypts" from becoming too
easy to build.

If you don't believe that these are problems - and I think they
are relatively small problems given the existing cardsets and the
likely availability of vampires in the future - then grouping is
a bad idea. But quitting the game over it seems kind of like
cutting off your nose to spite your face. It's not like you can't
keep playing with your existing vampires and crypts. You just
wouldn't be able to mix in the highest-group vampires with some
of the vampires you already own.

Group 4 seems like it would be annoying because there would probably
be only a few vampires in group 4 and they could only be used with
group 3 vampires. This is quite a bit like the situation when
Dark Sovereigns came out - there were only the original-set vamps,
and then you got a few more vamps to add to them for the Camarilla
clans in DS. It's just that we're so far past that point now that
people would find it frustrating to have so *little* crypt diversity
available in the new grouping combination.

And I do think that grouping rules are probably a lot more bad than
good for the game overall; since there's so much existing availability
of vampires with particular disciplines already - especially at the
lower capacity levels - adding more duplication seems like much less
harm than pissing off a significant number of players by not allowing
new vampires to mix with the old ones.

Still, I'm not quitting the game over it. :-)

Josh

I know we're not supposed to post just to say me, too. But these last
three paragraphs express my point of view pretty accurately. I would
add one thing to your last sentence however: White Wolf has to give
players a good reason to buy new cards even if they don't quit the game
over it right away. Why does anyone want to buy a vampire they can't
use very often? There aren't enough group three vampires out now to
justify group fours, not by a long shot.

it would get bought as a set. Perhaps it will. I still hate getting
cards you can't use in amongst the useful stuff, though. And I also
think at some point, you have to look at whether you're needlessly
irritating people.

Messages.Body:

If you look at it there are almost as many group 3 as group 1 vampires. 15
from each clan (-1 clan) and no Catieff (but there are Sabbat in CE so it's
pretty much a wash). So there are aproximitly even numbers of group 1 and 3
vampires currently. How many vamps would you say is enough for group 3?
Group 1 has 125 (ballpark) and group 2 has 300 (ballpark), how many group 3
should we get Fred? Group 2 is the biggest group by far. It seems that
keeping group 1 and group 3 the same size would be a logical idea as they
both have access to group 2. One could speculate that grouping could follow
a pattern: small group, big group, small, big.... and so on. If that
pattern were followed you would have access to aprox 400 vampires in any

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Dave Brereton wrote:
>
> Frederick Scott <freds64_at_...@removethis.com> wrote in message
> news:3DC1642C...@removethis.com...
> > There aren't enough group three vampires out now to
> > justify group fours, not by a long shot.
>
> If you look at it there are almost as many group 3 as group 1 vampires.

I realize that. But that's not a workable criterion. The problem is the
utility of a group 4 vampire both in a pure sense and in relation to other
vampires. Actually, the latter is what I truly care about but I concede
it's a bit unfair: the utility of a given group of vampires must necessarily
change over time as new vampires in the same group and adjoining groups are
printed. So I included the "in a pure sense" version to express the point
that it's only right to print a card that has at least *minimal* utility
even as it's printed - even if you promise to make it more useful later.

In either case, the question is about how many potential crypt-fellows a
group 4 vampire as it gets printed, not whether there's balance between
groups 1 and 3. Group 1 and 3 vampires have all of group 2 to play with
which, is a much larger group than group 3. Group 2 vampires have everything
until new group 4s come out. Of course, there's a question of how likely
you are to use, say, a group 1 vampire with a group 2 vampire given that
they are often if different clans. So it's not really possible to compare
the two situations.

So the answer to your question is that it's a thoroughly subjective. But
Josh's statement was on the money: any Group 4 vampire coming out at this
point will be subject to so little diversity in its use that people will
find it frustrating (to own).

> One could speculate that grouping could follow
> a pattern: small group, big group, small, big.... and so on. If that
> pattern were followed you would have access to aprox 400 vampires in any
> combination of groups. If Group 3 never gets another vampire it would allow
> as many as 4 ( most likley 3) expansions to be released with group 4
> vampires. That's a lot of expansions! I like expansions!

Sure. The *problem* with that view is that until more expansions come out,
the usefulness of the early vampires printed in it will tend to suck.

Fred

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <3DC17F10...@removethis.com>, Frederick Scott

<freds64_at_...@removethis.com> writes:
>In either case, the question is about how many potential crypt-fellows a
>group 4 vampire as it gets printed

As has been pointed out, in a very real sense, things like the Ravnos
were in a league of their own when printed - a whole 10 vampires who you
could basically play with themselves or not at all.

Sasha, can't cross unless you're just looking for 2 cap weenies.

Tsigane, poor cross unless you *really* want Auspex weenies. (At the
time, why? And even now, inferior Auspex wouldn't be great.)

Salbatore Bokkengro - for/pro at 4 capacity. Ricki and Roman would be
better choices, possibly Chandler (who came out in DS)

(You could, conceivably, be SalBok a number of the above in Trap/Undead
Persistence decks, but these weren't particularly well explored at the
time.)

Andre - getting too big to cross over just for the ani/for. Where does
the Celerity fit in? Smallest ani/for/cel was Quinton
McDonnell. (Potential ani/for/cel/chi with Constantin.)

Joaquina - first non-Chimerstry superiors - ANI CHI FOR, with a +1
stealth equip. So with Ani/For you go to the Gangrel again. At
5 they have Raven and Camille (though at the time, many people
played them as the same vampire) with ani/FOR/PRO, Bear Paw with
ANI for pro; at 6, Zack with ani/for/pro/+1 strength and Badger
with ani FOR PRO. So yes, the cheapest source of ANI FOR
(Sarisha Veliku competes in AH), but not a stupendously good
cross-over. Superior Animalism gave you +1 life on a number of
retainers, Drawing out the Beast's damage at superior, optional
presses with Conquer the Beast (a very poor card), destroy
equipment with Canine Horde (better now than it was, equipment
being very poor and unused), intercept from Cat's Guidance, not
just untap (one of the best flexible cats in the set at the
time), nothing on Army of Rats, a press on Aid from Bats (if you
weren't getting pinged by S:CE, that's not bad) and Rats Warning
(usable, but better for the Nosferatu/Spawning Pool).
Shepherd's Innocence, introduced in Dark Sovereigns, gives you a
very powerful steal card, but it's focused only at Animalism -
you need other people to be playing Animalism, and you need to
be able to get the action through, which is difficult if the
Animalism cards on the table are Raven Spy with a cat guiding
them for backup.

There were, in fact, days before Carrion Crows and my love for
the card. The only downside to Carrion Crows is that Gratiano
can't play it.

Vaclav - ANI CHI for pot. Well, the Potence might work reasonably well
in a Nosferatu deck. At 6, he's a cheap source of ANI pot
(Nigel and Calebros are cheaper, but aren't available right
now). Unfortunately, ani/pot was generally regarded as pants
relative to cel/pot and obf/pot, both potent forces. With only
ANI/for, the Gangrel are really outclassing him at this point,
unless you desperately need ANI. Only Bear Paw (5) has ANI for,
neither of the sixes do, then you hit Gunther and Gitane. But
you're probably using Protean too at that size.

Natalia - +1 bleed, dom/for. Conceivably, that's a Ventrue deck. They
don't have +1 bleed that small. But they do have DOM/FOR/PRE
and titles at 7 capacity (Walter the Sweaty), though you could
try some bizarre Animalism tag-team with Timothy Crowley. The
Dominate works not badly with new Ravnos and stuff, but it
didn't transfer well outside the clan back then.

Tereza Rostas - with only FOR and three inferiors, 8 capacity is getting
big. Ani/Aus isn't a big thing at the time, no Tzimisce,
smallest is Thomas Thorne at 6. Ani/For/Pot/Aus. A Sheldon
tag-team, maybe. Except Sheldon has ANI AUS for POT at 9
capacity, and three votes. Still, the FOR might come in handy.
But you're really getting too big to not be using a special
ability heavily (hers is pants) or lots of disciplines.

Darius - with FOR/PRO/ani, and a fairly neat special - you get to see a
card anyway - you could make a potentially convincing argument
(even if you decided against it) for him to go in a Gangrel
deck. But you have got competition from Gitane and Ingrid and
Katarina, not to mention Wynn for a mere 1 capacity point more,
with his built in rush. Doable, but not supremely pressing.

Kostantin - well, you've got ANI/dom/FOR, for that Timothy Crowley deck,
but it's not really that pressing. The steal equipment is nice
if it happens, but you can't plan for it, so you're unlikely to
put him in a deck thinking "Yes, I will bring him out and steal
equipment and rule the world." That celerity isn't really
making him a big out of clan fiend either.

So, none of them are super, extra special madly needed out of clan,
though you could make a case for some in some decks, just about. Who,
if you're playing Ravnos, are you going to bring *into* the clan to mix?
You're picking up a lot of Chimerstry, so maybe a few small ani/for
types to weenify the deck slightly, using the bigger vampires for
Sensory Deprivation. Use some ani for intercept retainers, maybe, and
Fortitude to defend something. Maybe you have the Rack out and want it
defended - the Ravnos were in dire problems with blood gain after all.
They (the ani/for intruders) could use the Computer Hackings you put in
for a bleed angle, but not the Fata Morgana you were using both for
stealth *and* for bleed (if you had CHI).

So how many decks could you seriously lend them to? And how many could
you seriously get loans from? Not really very many at all. They were a
clan without "many potential crypt-fellows". How many people quit the
game because the Ravnos were printed though? I can't remember any for
that reason. The V:TES angle, yes. The Ravnos angle? Not that I can
recall.

Later, with Ancient Hearts, you get Lazar Dobrescu - a very nice snaffle
for the Ventrue or the Gangrel, to be honest. Sarisha - well, maybe you
*can* do something with ANI/dom/FOR. You've got a small cluster now -
Natalia, Timothy, Sarisha. Worth a go, perhaps. Still no Carrion Crows
for Animalism fun when blocked on a bleed, though. You have to rely on
Scorpion Sting (just came in), maybe, or Aid from Bats, pinging at them
and preventing any damage to you, and throwing down Conditioning when
they don't block. Doable, perhaps, at the time. Petru Sipos - well,
the SER is incompatible with the Setites - nothing else makes him cross
over. Stealing blood in torpor? Well, if you can get them to torpor,
maybe. Slow, too. Might as well just hit them into torpor and use
Taste of Vitae. Not a fantastic vampire for matching up crypt-mates.

Yet I still don't know anyone who quit because the Ravnos were printed,
even though they had extremely limited crypt-mate potential, even after
3 extra vampires were printed for them.

--

This is certainly true. But there you did have 10 new vampires who
went together as a clan, with their "new clan skill" to lend them
interest. If we were to get, say, 3 vampires for each Camarilla
clan in Group 4 in Anarchs, you would only have 3 vamps that went
together for any one clan - so the only time you'd want to use Group
4 vamps instead of Group 2 vamps for any particular deck is if those
specific Group 4 guys fit *so well* into your deck idea that they'd
be better than any number of Group 2 guys.

The situation only gets "worse" (or "harder to use" or "more narrow")
if there are fewer than 3 vamps per Cam clan, too.

If there were 10, that'd probably be enough to make them pretty usable.
That would require some 60 slots devoted to Cam vamps, though, which
might be an awful lot for what may be a fairly small set.

Josh

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <aps4ml$4jp4u$1...@ID-121616.news.dfncis.de>, Joshua Duffin

<jtdu...@yahoo.com> writes:
>This is certainly true. But there you did have 10 new vampires who
>went together as a clan, with their "new clan skill" to lend them
>interest. If we were to get, say, 3 vampires for each Camarilla
>clan in Group 4 in Anarchs, you would only have 3 vamps that went
>together for any one clan - so the only time you'd want to use Group
>4 vamps instead of Group 2 vamps for any particular deck is if those
>specific Group 4 guys fit *so well* into your deck idea that they'd
>be better than any number of Group 2 guys.

The very obvious alternative is that a different theme (or themes) is
explored.

Instead of, say, having Fortitude as a common out of clan discipline for
<Clan X>, you give the new vampires Celerity instead, creating a new
niche.

Compare Euro-Brujah. You wouldn't use them - in Dark Sovereigns -
because they were so much better than your Group One (V:TES) vampires,
per se. You'd use them because they worked entirely differently to your
group one vampires.

Of course, bit DOM/POT at the time was *potentially* usable with the
Giovanni. But, like the Ravnos, you'd find the inclusion of Necromancy
on most of the Giovanni would mean that the Dominate/Potence angle would
be slightly watered down, and for 8 pool, that's a lot of 'waste' you've
got there.

At this point, you don't have to make them *better* than the group 2
vampires, you just change the focus. Group 2 has <x> so let's give
these <!x>. Say, instead of Brujah with Dominate as a little cluster,
create, say, a cluster of Brujah with Dementation. (No-one has it so
far.) Or give the Toreador a big Animalism side-line, maybe a splash of
Vic on one of them. (Ira Rivers, [3], has ani. Alexandra [2] has ANI.)
Maybe throw the Ventrue some Necromancy, as well as dom/for/pre. How
about a cluster of Independent Ventrue, calling Free States Rant?
Ventrue Headquarters in play, maybe even an Assembly. And these
Necromancing Ventrue upstarts, having got into business with the
Giovanni, manage to get the nasty vampires hunted down by the Society of
Leopold and then raise them from the dead. Or Tremere with Serpentis,
letting you, err, accelerate the usage of Temptation.

Would any of those be useful? Perhaps, perhaps not. Obviously, you'd
want to play-test and find useful canon vampires or get White Wolf to
'invent' some and so on. But they wouldn't be *better* than group 2.
Donal and Constanza and Volker would still kick ass, just as they do
now. But the Dementation Brujah would be able to do very different
things.

> > until now they have heeded our thoughts and needs, more or less, so we have

...

> Like I said so many times already, if your playgroup agrees, just
> ignore the grouping rules! That is what we are doing here and doing
> fine. Even the Camarilla-Clan haters don´t complain.

Without endorsing Orpheus's campaign, I really think your reply is hardly an
answer for it. One can do anything desired with one's own cards, it's true.
But with a game, you need like-minded people to do it. The shortcomings of
"house rule" play, even when the house rules are fairly obvious, are well-
documented: aside from the lack of tournament and tournament prize support,
you deprive yourself of experience in the "real" game and thus - to some
extent - cut yourself out of tournaments that exist that are supported by
the central organization. You also make it difficult to play in non-
tournament environments you run into while traveling. And CCGs have a much
more serious issue in this sense than, say, board games or RPGs. CCGs
involve deckbuilding, so you automatically create a serious inconvenience
for yourself if you choose to jump back and forth between different
environments. You can't just "forget one set of rules" and start playing
by the other. You have to have separate decks built (or are somehow
convertible on location) which are appropriate for each environment you
play in.

On a completely different tact, all the cards that get printed over time
are designed, playtested, and are ultimately finalized under only one
environment. I realize the grouping rule is somewhat subtle in terms of
its balance issues, so I'm not sure any obvious problems caused by this
will arise. (At least not soon, I would expect.) But over time, it might
cause problems. And if it does, you can bet that the incentives for the
designers to fix these will hover long about zero, as their obvious
response to any such problems would be: "Use the real rules we give you."

I wouldn't discourage you from doing anything you like that allows you to
have fun with your cards. I just wanted to point out that the fact the
grouping rule exists and is now part of the game is truly important. Like
it or not, we now have to live with it and treat its implications as
serious ones, whether any local group uses them or not.

> No amount of ranting and/or arguments until now have seemed to work with
> WW. So your boicott will probably be ignored.

That might be true. I do think expressing displeasure about what they do
when you can do so with good reasoning ultimately has an effect, though.
And I don't think you can nor should wave your hand over the effects of
the grouping rule so easily.

Fred

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:

> WoD storyline. Having the DS/AH titled Gangrel mixing with the new
> Anarch Gangrel just seems wrong to me.

Why is that? There were the group one set of Camarilla vampires that
can mix with the group two Camarillas which, in turn, can be mixed with
the group three Camarilla vampires. Although Gangrel are now
independent (for really silly storyline reasons :-{, but that's a
different subject), their clan is really spaced the same way as the
Camarilla clans. So it seems totally reasonable that a new set of 10
Group three Gangrel is precisely what's called for. Group fours would
not be able to mix with Group twos, which is certainly unfair compared
to the other six original clans.

I realize this would allow for Cammie Gangrel mixed with independent
Gangrel, but I'm not sure that's as strange as all that. I think one
would expect the process of pulling the Gangrel out of the Camarilla
would not be an instantaneous thing, anyway. Such a crypt would seem to
represent a set of conservative and radical Gangrel mixing during the
changeover.

> Perhaps this is a way they're
> fixing that problem. Granted, they won't have access to the 372 Group
> 2 vampires, but in my experience, the Gangrel didn't mix a whole lot
> with other clans, aside from the odd Malkavian Madness Network Table

Perhaps. They do mix fairly well with other Gangrel however.

> I certainly hope they DO take their time (except perhaps with one more
> expansion). I think very few people want to recycle their entire
> collections every 2 years.

Actually, I agree with all that (accepting the concept that grouping is a
good thing at all notwithstanding) except for the part about Anarchs. As
you point out, there are more group one vampires than current group threes.
The reason for this is exactly because there aren't currently any Gangrel
or any Caitiff, as there were in group one. These are precisely the subject
matter for Anarchs, are they not? Hence, one would expect to find them
also in group three. And if anything, group three ought to be larger than
group one just because it would make the stress of the changeover to group
four easier.

There really ought to be a better way to this. To me, it would make more
sense to wait until the next large expansion containing many independent
vampires to start group four in bulk. Starting it as part of a small
expansion featuring vampires that, by all rights, ought to be group three
seems very strange. Not very well thought out, IMO.

Fred

Hi again all,
rather than answering many times to each of you I'll just try to answer on
the whole.

- First, I'm not really "campaining", as I don't run for elections and don't
expect anything for my personnal profit here. I just protest in my name and
the name of many players I know, because I want this game to stay what we
love, and not to become progressively just another soulless commercial
machine. I have nothing to win except the pleasure to see the game stay the
way I deem best, and I put my Princehood on the stake (I am a man of word,
and will do what I said no matter what) ; I also wanted to express what I
think is the PoV of many players, but judging from your answers I may be
mistaken, lots of you don't seem to care.

- I didn't threaten to quit the game, Josh, just to stop buying and
promoting it. You can't do something you don't believe in anymore, can you ?
As of now, I still believe in this game, I'm just stating what will make me
so disgusted I will have to quit. I will probably still play it (have enough
cards to last me a century), but it won't give anymore more money to WW? so
if enough people say the same it will give them something to think about.

- Just ignoring the Group rules isn't a solution IMO because it won't be
allowed in tournaments, and the game balance will be thought out with these
rules in mind. Someone spoke of Brujah with Dem as opposed to Euro-Brujahs ?
What if the group 4 give 5 new Brujahs with Dom ? 6 more Malks with Pre ?
Etc. It just won't be worth playing Sabbat (or fucking Bloodlines !!!)
anymore if your Cammie opponents can chose from 324 (random number)
vampires, so you cannot just ignore grouping.

- The reason "new players can't get their hands on old vampires" isn't
valid. Old vampires can be reprinted, as they did with Group 2 in starters
(even though most group 2 vampires stink and we could have done without,
except for the freaks who want to try the dreaded qui/pro/tha combo, for
example...). Good reasons for creating groups are : 1) we want to make new,
better vampires than in the original edition without giving too big of an
edge to Camarilla, and 2) we want to change who owns the titles (but then
why reprint the old Inner Circle ?!), and as Joshua just said, even that is
a half-valid reason. Bad reason is : we want to sell new cards, and don't
care about the players, so we make lots of vampires not playable together,
and sod'em all. I hope that's not the whole of the thing, and that's why I'm
making this plea (turning into a War Cry) to WW.

- Let's be clear : we don't NEED any new groups. I'd agree with the one
saying that new discipline combos would be interesting, but that wouldn't
justify a new group (who cares if there are 4 new Brujahs with Dem but
without their 3 basic disciplines, they wouldn't count as 4 more Brujahs or
as 4 more Malks, it's a whole new thing !!). As long as there are as many
new Sabbat / Cammies / Indies, there can be lots of them without it creating
any problem. The only ones who will suffer are Bloodlines, except of course
if some new vampires from other Clans include their disciplines. But anyway,
they won't suffer less with a Group 4 (not mixeable with them at all).

- Now, Group 4 Sabbat and Indies would mean : all your old Sabbatics and
Indies are to be thrown away and replaced, OR there is no interest in buying
new vampires. It would stink, and there is no valid reason to this that I
can see. Same can be said with Group 5, which would render obsolete all the
new vampires that just came out. That, for me, would be the proof of the
"screw you" politics. And PLEASE don't tell me that old vampires would still
be tournament legal, we all know where it will end if we start on that road
(for some people the thing is already done with Group 3, for others it will
be with Group 4 ; I say some damage has been done but it's not a killing
blow yet ; please stop it theren though !!).

Did I forget anything ?

Yes : please speak up, all who think that Group 4 Cammies are THE limit to
what can be done without killing our game !!!

Orpheus

Apart from the deckbuilding issues you put forth, not using the
grouping rule is hardly a "house rule". When you play any given game

combinations within your own crypt, not within the game table.
Vampires from non-compatible groups can by the "real rules" be in a
same game, even a same methuselah愀 controlled area, if he manages to
steal or borrow them. So the game already conforms 100% to using all
and/or any vampires in a given game. Not using the grouping rule would
only affect your deckbuilding, and nothing else in the game. After the
game starts, 0% of the rules have to be changed or ignored. So it愀
not really a house rule. You get my point here? I HATE house rules. I
really do. This is just using all the "real cards" with the "real
rules", only building the crypt anyway we want to (again, conforming
to all the other "real rules"). If limiting your crypt is limiting
your fun or enjoyment of the game, don愒 limit it.

rule isn愒 as complicated or difficult to do like you make it sound.

pointing out to them that for now, you can so easilly ignore it that
it should be no reason to quit the game for. Not using the grouping
rule is about as "wrong" as thinking you ALWAYS have to play exactly

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Daniel Figueiredo wrote:
> Apart from the deckbuilding issues you put forth, not using the
> grouping rule is hardly a "house rule". When you play any given game
> of V:TES, the grouping rule only prohibits you to use certain group
> combinations within your own crypt, not within the game table.
> Vampires from non-compatible groups can by the "real rules" be in a

> same game, even a same methuselah´s controlled area, if he manages to

> steal or borrow them. So the game already conforms 100% to using all
> and/or any vampires in a given game. Not using the grouping rule would
> only affect your deckbuilding, and nothing else in the game. After the

> game starts, 0% of the rules have to be changed or ignored. So it´s

> not really a house rule. You get my point here?

Actually, I do not. All the facts you give are true but irrelevant.
Lots of things are possible across a table that are not possible within
one's own area. For instance, using Goth Band to move a counter from
an opponent's Dreams of the Sphinx to your own Palla Grande doesn't make
it meaningless to change the rules to allow moving counters from your
_own_ Dreams to your own Palla Grande. What types of crypts are allowed
and not allowed determine the makeup of your metagame, which makes it
undeniably a different game. (See more discussion of the metagame
issues below if you don't understand what I'm saying, here.)

Any rules that are not the official rules are _by definition_ "House
Rules". Denying this is a semantic argument. If you don't agree with
my definition, call them anything you like. Call them "BIDZUNK RULES"
or "COYFERTBURGER RULES" or use any term you like. It doesn't matter.
The point I'm trying to make is simply that they're different from the
universal rules that are understood in other places. By virtue of this
fact, in turn, *automatically* leads to all the issues I raised in my
previous post. These are serious issues and that leads me to conclude
that simply ignoring any potential problems caused partially by the
grouping rule by ignoring grouping itself is not an answer to them.

> However, you do make correct points on just about everything else
> you said. Mainly about how you would have to change your deck (just
> your crypt most of the time) when going from environment to

> environment. But it´s not like we shift environments that much (at
> least most of us don´t), and when we do, It will probably be to play
> in a tournament. And the opportunity to play V:TES doesn´t just pop

> out of the ground like that. So almost always, we will have time to
> make such changes to our decks. My point is, ignoring the grouping

> rule isn´t as complicated or difficult to do like you make it sound.

It may not be where you play. However, if you live somewhere where
you would wind up popping back and forth between the two constantly,
it gets a lot more irritating. And personally, I really would never
want to play by house rules (or Coyfertburger Rules, if you will) just
because I don't have mental horsepower to keep with two different
game environments so I want to focus on the real one. Hell, I have
a hard enough time just trying to keep up with the one without
constantly falling on face. That, by itself, makes proposing such
rules a poor answer for (I suspect) many people.

> Not using the grouping
> rule is about as "wrong" as thinking you ALWAYS have to play exactly
> the same way, wanting everyone else to play exactly the same way or
> not play at all. The game gets played exactly the same with no
> grouping rule (for now, as no card or effect affects or pertains to
> the grouping rule).

I disagree, due to the metagame issues I referred to above. As certain
decks become viable under your rules that would be illegal under the
grouping rules, this affects all other decks in your metagame, whether
legal under grouping rules or not. Grouping-legal decks that might be
pointless to play under grouping rules may take on a critical role in
a non-grouping environment and vice versa. Because of this, the game is
actually *not* "played exactly the same with no group rule".

> > > No amount of ranting and/or arguments until now have seemed to work with
> > > WW. So your boicott will probably be ignored.
> >
> > That might be true. I do think expressing displeasure about what they do
> > when you can do so with good reasoning ultimately has an effect, though.
> > And I don't think you can nor should wave your hand over the effects of
> > the grouping rule so easily.
>
> What effect has expressing our displeasure had until now? Zip.

...

> WW has not said a word about why or how they made the changes did they?
> Did they try to explain what their thought process was? Did they try to
> point out future developments of the game that would greatly benefit from
> the changes they have made? No.

I think you make a lot of assumptions that may or may not be valid. No,
they did not visibly react to complaints about the layout nor the grouping
rules, if that's what you mean. That doesn't completely invalidate the
concept that it's pointless to complain. First of all, by the time we
discovered about these things, it was too late anyway. They were not
going to recall card already printed. Granted, it wasn't a "good thing",
IMHO, to spring this on us but it still doesn't automatically imply that
complaining is pointless. Even if they didn't care to change their minds
about some things, it doesn't mean they'll never change their minds about
anything else based on various forms of customer feedback. Such a policy
would be insane. I believe feedback on past issues has made a number of
differences. For example, I notice they didn't use the rarity scheme from
Final Nights that I and some others complained about in either Bloodlines
or Camarilla Edition. (That was about there being a very few R1s in a set
containing many R2s, which gives the feeling of "super-rares".) It might
be coincidence, as no one has ever promised not to repeat the practice.
But it might not be.

Does this all mean it is or is not pointless to complain about cards in
Anarchs being printed in group four? (Assuming the rumor is even true,
of course.) I couldn't say. But I'm pretty sure it doesn't hurt to try,
as long as the comments are constructive.

> They even ignored any and all questions regarding
> any decision of theirs in the CE expansion during the developer chat.

"Ignored"? I think you mean that they didn't answer such questions, which
is not the same thing. They don't want to expose how various kinds of
decisions get made for various reasons. I don't know what those reasons
are, exactly. But I might speculate that sometimes they have to do with
not wanting to state who has what kinds of input into what kinds of
decisions so that those exact people needn't come under undue scrutiny and
pressure by the customer population. If we know such-and-such a person
makes decisions about card rarity levels and an expansion comes out in
which certain rarity decisions are rather unpopular, sometimes people have
been known to start making very personal comments about that person. Many
of us loved to hate Ryan Dancy, for example, because we knew various stuff
about what he had control over which we didn't like the results. A *lot*
of unflattering things got said about Ryan. Ryan was an executive,
however - prepared to take the credit and the blame for the decisions he
made. I have little doubt that Steve Wieck receives input on all kinds of
things that might not have popular outcomes from people he doesn't want to
get caught in the middle of huge flamewars taking personal blows. Hence,
when asked how various decisions get made, exactly, the reply is likely to
be, "No comment...". It's what I'd do.

None of this means they never listen. They may listen or they may not.
If they do listen, they may be persuaded or they may not. I know they
will never be persuaded if we don't talk.

Fred

Messages.Author: Thomas Pichler
Messages.Body:
Orpheus wrote:
> I, Orpheus, Prince of Marseille, France, hereby declare that if any

> comes out, I will :
>
> - stop buying new products
> - resign from my Princeship

What's the point?

The grouping rule has its advantages - changes to Majesty et al. aside,
would you really want pre weenie decks to have yet another X unique
vampires of capacities 1-4 available? Or how about pot weenies? Or how
about 12 different Ventrue princes (and in the long run, 8 of those with
obfuscate, too)? Or...

It is, however, a question of whether or not the arrival of yag (yet
another group) is sensibly timed.
Personally I'd say, that particular line would be pretty much crossed by
any group 4 vampires in The Anarchs, unless The Anarchs would be huge
enough a set to have 3+ group 4 vampires per clan that gets any.
[Effectivly being a DS replacement for CE.]

There should be group 4 Independent/Sabbat vampires eventually - several
Sabbat decks, for example, would gain too powerful a crypt if another
Sabbat set with 15 vampires (goup 3) came out.

There'd even have to be group 5 vampires some time down the road, when
all group 3/4 option (and those are aplenty) are exhausted - it doesn't
need to happen for a few years yet, and consequently shouldn't happen
for a few years, but it'll be inevitable in the long run. (At 8 month
intervals between sets and 4 sets [Anarchs, Sabbat, Independent, next
Cammie], 32 months would be a quick estimate.)

I'll be basing my personal decision on if/when to quit buying VTES on
these considerations.

Thomas

most sold in France (I'm not considering Pokemon which is not the same
marketing target). Expansions after expansions, WotCoast introduced a nasty
selling system with Type1 and Type2. Tournaments are now almost exclusively
played in Type 2. The definition of Type 2 is : a combination between the
last 3 or 4 expansions sold in store.

By this way, regarding the frequency of new expansions apparition, players
wanting to play in tournaments are OBLIGED to buy new expansions to stay at
the level.

NOTHING can let us think such a commercial way will NOT be attempted when we
will have groupe 4, 5, 6, which could occur, cause Vtes is well-sold around
the world (dixit WW ceo...).

As it is well-sold, it must be encouraged that way, taken care of. That is
what the game brainers are doing (thank you LSJ...) by being there to answer
to players, to introduce a community aspect in the game etc... But the
commercial and marketing departments, in order to have the game grow, need
to improve the sales. This is called the Raisonnement Marginal in economy
(in french. Dunno the translation. Will never work in US -( ).

SO, it is POSSIBLE, in few years, as the game will sales better again, that,
in order to sale it better, such a "magic-style" tournament rule appears,
letting us play only with some group vampires. In this case, we will be
OBLIGED to buy expansions.

As nothing of this could merely happen if no other group 5 and more are
sold, I think it is clever to tell WW that some people want to buy
expansions, merely if they are well designed like those ones we have got for
the moment, but don't want to be obliged to buy them.

One more time again, I'm just talking about a correlation to Orpheus'
reflexion, and I thought people should think of that.

Vtes won't live forever if it doesn't succeed in acquiring new players.
Let's think what are the ways a CCG company has got to get them, and for
that, look at the competitors' marketing actions, as companies often copy on
each other.

Arpeges (ready for Derek's flame)

> Rules". Denying this is a semantic argument. If you don't agree with
> my definition, call them anything you like. Call them "BIDZUNK RULES"
> or "COYFERTBURGER RULES" or use any term you like. It doesn't matter.

> universal rules that are understood in other places. By virtue of this
> fact, in turn, *automatically* leads to all the issues I raised in my
> previous post. These are serious issues and that leads me to conclude

> grouping rule by ignoring grouping itself is not an answer to them.

Well, you may be right in THEORY, but in practice, when we play,
group and no group rule has made no difference yet. And don´t think we
wouldn´t know. We´ve been playing this game from day 1. And I never
said anything about not using grouping rules in tournaments, as prince
I always use 100% official rules, be the tournaments sacntioned or
not. I am also not trying to discuss the merit of the grouping rule.
It exists. Too bad, or great, whatever. I am fully aware of the
implications of the group rule in the present game, and have as good
idea as you do about any implications it might have in the future.

I´ll try once more to get my point(s) across. Please remember that
English is not my native tongue so don´t be mad if you don´t get it,
it is probably just my fault for not using the best words for
expressing myself.

1) We have the grouping rule.
2) We always use it in competitive play.
3) 90% of the time we don´t play competitively (I guess most people
don´t most of the time either)
4) Yes, it is good to express our opinions about the game, whether WW
listens, does something about it or not. (If they are listening and/or
doing something about it, they should let us know don´t you think? Not
WHAT they are doing if the don´t want to, but at least that they ARE
doing something).
5) Not using the grouping rule has not yet affected any of our games,
and we play once a week at least, and most of us have bought at least
a booster or 10 from the CE.
6) We have decided that for now, we will play like this because it is
more fun and enjoyable. Someone in some recent post mentioned nothing
would keep him from using his favourite vampires. RIGHT ON!!
7) We are not ignoring any problems because we haven´t found any that
are really happening yet, like I said, in practice, not using the
grouping rule has led to nothing but more diverse crypts.
8) I agree with you that the group thing CAN and probably will become
a problem in the future.
9) Fact remains that WW is either not listening or not letting us know
that it is. Of course, how could they know we would react the way we
did to the CE? They not only weren´t listening, they didn´t ask our
opinion and/or thoughts about what they were about to do.

I understand what you said about WW wanting to avoid problems with
their people getting pressure from the players if they started to open
all doors. but they don´t have to name names. They really don´t. All
they need to do is say We, WW, are planning to do this and that, or
We, WW WILL be doing this and that, or We, WW would like to know your
thoughts on such and such. We can all guess that Steve and LSJ have
some influence, probably a lot in the decision-making process. I don´t
see hardly anyone flamimg them though. First, it would be childish to
do so. (yes, some players would, and have done, childish things, but
they will do them regardless) Second, it would probably be the most
counter-productive thing we can do. To start criticising WW employees
about their job if they ever DO decide to share who they are with us.
It would probably just make them shut up again and leave us in the
dark (where we are now). The changes to rarity schemes WW has made
until now probably have nothing to do with complaints from people
here. It has probably something to do with the fact that this is WW´s
first card game, and they are experimenting with various rarity
schemes. Every expansion of theirs until now had different ones. Every
expansion has met some form of criticism regarding rarity schemes. Are
they changing because of us? I don´t think so. I think they are
changing to find something they are comfortable with, and maybe,
something that won´t get flamed (highly unlikely due to the
aformentioned childish players). but like I said, we are in the dark
about all this. WW´s not commenting, not asking questiongs and not
shedding any light on their thoughts. I hope you are right in thinking
that this is best for the game. I really do.

Some more cents (soon we´ll have a dolar!)
And i´m very pleased to be discussing with sharp minds and educated
people. :))

insulted me), but we don't seem to speak the same language (but then, I'm no
english native). I don't want to ruin anything for anybody. My only goal is
to express an opinion, which many players here and elsewhere share, and to
try to change things from within, to keep alive the game I and these people
love. Is saying that we don't want new groups popping up on a regular basis
"ruining" anything for anyone ?? I'm ready (and willing !) to buy whole new
inventive extensions for Jyhad (even if they are not compatible at all with
the old extension, like a Dark Age version) as long as I will feel that it
will bring something new and interesting to the game, and not be motivated
only by commercial purposes. Playing Dark Ages versions of the Lasombra is
one thing, playing modern Times Lasombra and not be able to play Gratiano or
Lucita would royally suck. And if I have to chose between new Lasombras, no
matter how overpowered, and these characters from the novels and books of
WW, my choice is already done. Does that example make my PoV clearer to you
? Also, I already pointed out that I would find it silly and disgusting to
render obsolete vampires that just got reprinted, hence my desire not ever
to see Group 4 Indies or Sabbat (Bloodlines would be worse than anything, as
they could need some more help, and not a variation of crypt). Yeah, I know,
you can still play the old vampires in different groups. Right. So why
bother buying the new ones ? I'm no Rockfeller, and if I bought so many
vampires I intend to play them as long as I enjoy it (and I hope that will
be a very long time), including new guys, but not throwing all the old ones
away. Group 3 Cammies I could understand, for me that's qhere it's got to
stop.

they issued new groups, did I ? I just said my involvment as a consumer and
a promoter of the game would stop, and that I thought (and hoped, for I hate
blind followers) that I wouldn't be the only one to react so. Does this
hamper in any way your freedom to spend all your money for Group 6 Austin
Circle Blood Brothers ? Methinks not.

see why I could want such a thing). But I won't ruin myself buying cards I
don't need just because of an intelligent but disgusting commercial
strategy. I just hope WW will not take this turn for the worse.

Orpheus

persuaded the next time. It's that simple. You seem to keep trying to
read into their actions more than what these actions actually prove.

> expansion has met some form of criticism regarding rarity schemes. Are
> they changing because of us? I don´t think so.

I don't see how you come to that conclusion. Of course they make mistakes.
Determining the popular rarity for cards is another one of the many
subjective things in a CCG and certainly impossible to ever please
everybody. And each of their four expansions has been printed under
completely different conditions, attempting to do completely different
things. Sabbat War was a kind-of, sort-of, mostly reprint of The Sabbat
with a few new cards. Final Nights was a balls-out expansions of the
independent clans. Camarilla Edition was intended as a new base set.
And Bloodlines was completely different than everything else. Of course
they make changes every time. I don't know if they listen to what we
say, but I'm pretty well impressed by how they've avoided what I would
personally consider the worst mistakes. Just for that alone, I'm willing
to give them the benefit of the doubt. There's companies out there that
act like "Blunder" is their middle name.

Fred

> subsequent attempts to correct the alleged inconsistancies by the NJL
> and other parties, have be incorporated into the current game play in
> bits and pieces. Not 100% mind you, but it happened.

Which ones are you thinking of?

The only complaint made by the NJL that has been addressed (off the top of
my head; please add in any I've missed) was the complaint about errata, and
"cards don't do what they say they do" making it difficult for new players.

NOBODY disagreed with the premise -- of course it'd be nice to play a game
where the cards did what they said! But if you recall, when the 7/7
rulings were issued, WotC was still in control of the game and there were
going to be NO new printings. It was either play a broken game, or issue
errata. Given that choice, the game was preserved with errata.

The demands of the NJL for no errata on the spot were unreasonable given the
current circumstances, and were correctly ignored. Once the circumstances
changed (WW took the game back over and printings started to happen again),
reprints of old cards matching the errata issued for those cards started to
happen -- WWEF being the first and most obvious.

> Player involvement CAN make a difference. It just has to be rational
> and fit within the game structure.

Yes, I agree completely. But the loud shouting and ranting created by 7/7
didn't accomplish a single thing. What accomplished far more was the
return of the game to White Wolf, where suddenly the entire baseline from
which to begin assessing things changed.

-- Derek

Well we first used something akin to the table win. We called it the
last man standing, which measured simply the ability of a player to have
staying power and that person of course always got 2 vps, which in the
current game setting usually means a table win.

as a % of wins.

many aspects of the game, these little bit seem to indicate that in our
breif heydey we were not simple making waves we actually help set the
template for the furture game.

Ok. The drugs are wearing off and the ego is deflating. :)
</ego>

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Peter Muto wrote:
>
> The reality is I think WW is brilliant. The thing is crypt cards and
> library cards are very very different; they have a very different
> function/utility to players. Here's the thing:
> IF WW instituted a "Type II" thing where all of a sudden my 15 Jyhad
> Flesh of Marble's are now kindling I'd freak out.

Most of my comments will be at the bottom. I had stop here and point
out, however, that you're obviously comparing apples with oranges.
No one proposed a "Type II" thing for library cards any more than
anyone proposed one for crypt cards. The analogous rules for library
cards would be to print group numbers on the library cards - like the
crypt cards - and invent some rule about which group-numbered library
cards could be used in the same library deck. As they say for vampires,
"You can *STILL* use your Flesh of Marbles...this is NOT like Type II,
after all...". Enjoy!

> BUT if I have to continually buy group 4, 5, 6 etc. vampires, even
> buying a vampire identical to older ones but with different names and
> group numbers, that's fine. WW has to make money, and create *some*
> incentive for players to buy cards. Remember, nearly EVERY SINGLE card
> EVER printed is tournament legal. That's impressive. Sure you can't
> mix a small group together but at this point, I'd guess less than 25%
> of all Magic cards every printed are legal. We have it good folks. I
> could even live with Jyhad vamps becoming illegal if they basically
> reprinted them all with different names and group #'s. Library cards
> are a different matter though, which is my point.
> Remember, crypt cards is not a card that you need millions of like
> some library cards. I mean the absolute most you would ever *need* of
> a vampire is 12 technically, realistically 2-6 of each vampire is
> plenty.

You've stated a bunch of true facts that miss the central point,
though. Variety of cards is power - period. This is every bit as true
of library cards as crypt cards. It doesn't matter how many library
library cards it takes to make a crypt. What matters is the ability
to combine different combinations of cards - for instance Aid from Bats
with Carrion Crows. Combinations of library cards are much more likely
than crypt cards to confer advantage to longer-time players if the
newbies can't get them. Note, I said *if*. Frequent reprinting of
key library cards actually tends to mute the advantage quite a bit to
prevent too much real advantage. But one can conclude that if the
newbie disadvantage is the sole reason for grouping, then you ought to
group library cards, too - rather than bothering to reprint any.

> I think the group thing strikes a perfect balance between encouraging
> new and old players to buy new cards, from every new set without
> alienating anyone too much (the people who over-react always
> over-react)

It's a balance. It's completely subjective to suggest it's a "perfect"
one. I guess I'm glad they didn't do it to library cards, though by
logic one would certain expect that, too.

> I think in the end the group thing has very little to do with
> preventing a "Dial-A-Crypt" scenario as I think others have pointed
> out that such a scenario would not "break" the game.

I'm not really sure what are saying, if not that the group thing is to
prevent D-A-C. It is not to sell vampire cards, certainly. They will
sell more new vampire cards by allowing the existing players to use new
vampires with their current vampires.

Fred

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:


I see. If that's what it is, then I have to say I'm against it. Or at
least, I'm against bothering to try and dredge up every old, forgotten
card and attempting to do something about it. Every single one of these
puppies is another card that has copies out in the card population that
don't do what they SAY they do. That's bad! It's one thing to errata
overpowered cards. (And let's not kid ourselves, folks. Reprinting is
scarcely better than errata.) It's quite another to take an underpowered
piece of wallpaper which is doing relatively little harm except serving
as a laughing stock and a good example of how NOT to design future cards
and turn it into a true negative.

This process is turning particularly obnoxious when only slight changes
are made to old cards, so it's hard to spot when one comes up in play.
We need to start asking ourselves: WHY do this? What is the point
supposed to be?!? It's beginning to seem like the game is being gripped
by overly rigid and anal retentive motives that can't let a past mistake,
however harmless, just lie there. Worse, I feel like the reprints I'm see
are getting rather spotty play-testing at times, leading to a worse game
rather than a better one - even if you don't count the inaccurate pieces
of cardboard in circulation, which I do.

Please, let's stop this!

Fred

Messages.Author: Karol Magda
Messages.Body:
<most of the post snip-ed, will adress only thing about library
grouping>

> And grouping vampires doesn't solve the analogous problem
> > in terms of library cards, which to me, it seems like a more pernicious
> > problem anyway.
>
> This is true, potentially. i think in the future, or past, it might be
> necessary to group library cards.

Definitely.

Take MtG Type 1 for instance. Only like 5 cards from each new set are
playable in that format. Slightly more are playable for Type 1.5 ,
even more for Extended , like 10-15 percent of a new set is playable
in Type 2 and lot of the cards are playable in Block Constructed (one
big and two small set with common theme both in backstory and card
mechanics).

<example>

If you add 100 new cards to base of 2000+ cards the impact of the 100
new cards is small unless you create power escalation curve. Which is
BAD thing (and even Wizards are aware of this as seen in current sets,
contrary to what many peoples seems to believe here)

</example>

I would not like to see that happen in V:TES. (insignificance of new
cards or power escalation) I am not saying it is happening now, it's
might start to be a problem in distant (or not so distant) future.

The Block Constructed type of tournaments are considered to be:

1) most balanced of constructed formats

-mainly because it's easier to catch possible broken combos in testing
where only 500 cards exists in format compared to 2000+ cards format

2) most popular of constructed formats (and yes Wizards do
polls/researchs and DO care about their customers)

-because many cards otherwise not playable in other constructed
formats are playable here (or biggest percentage of cards you buy are
actually playable besides in draft)

-new players can compete with old players

The extended format (where you can use cards from last 3-4 such
cycles) is also very popular (although sometimes not very balanced)

The problem is that even in extended cards phase out in T1 void.
(because it becomes impossible to balance it) The problem with block
constructed is that every two or so years the block changes
completely.

So is there any similarity between this and current V:TES situation ?

I believe it is.

Grouping of vampires basically creates kind of 'block constructed'
crypt but the catch is that no crypt 'cycle' phase out entirely (you
can STILL play with group 1 vampires). It also enables to print new
and interesting vampires which do have an impact (and think about how
many of new CE vampires would not have an impact if grouping rule
didn't existed)

Grouping of library cards would open vast posibilities for new cards
and abilities which do have an impact and are not broken (and it may
become a problem otherwise in (not so) distant future)

It would also combine the essence of two most popular MtG constructed
formats:

- Block Constructed with it's ability to use most of cards you buy in
actual game

- Extended with it's ability to choose from vast/different deck
archetypes

It would also solve newcomers vs old players issue:

Newbies would be able to compete with old players (because current
group block of library/crypt card would not be weaker or stronger than
previous one, just different one)

Assuming the content of each new group cycle would be interesting old
players WOULD buy the set (I definitely bought Camarilla because of
cool new cards not because of the power level of cards - I can still
win without single new CE card in my crypt or library) and they would
still be able to play with their old favourite decks in order to
invoke fear in hearts of fellows players.

Karol

choice of either not using my old vampires, or not buying new
vampires. You can't do both, unless you want to maintain two separate

personally, I don't see the claimed benefits that are supposed to
offset this huge limitation. Many people are ignoring the grouping

Why? What kind of trouble would that create?

>From my perspective, grouping reduces playability. It reduces the
>number of combinations of vampires that can go into a crypt, and

I have to point out that 'not increasing combinations' != 'reducing
the number of combinations'. You have just as many group 1 + 2 combos
as you did before, and in addition you have 2 + 3 combos. So you have
MORE combinations, not FEWER.

>personally, I don't see the claimed benefits that are supposed to
>offset this huge limitation. Many people are ignoring the grouping
>rules, and so far none of them report any problems. That may be
>evidence that White Wolf was simply incorrect in their assumptions
>that grouping was necessary.

The grouping rule is forward-looking, in that it addresses a problem
caused not by CE, but by future expansions. It's an accumulative thing --
I wouldn't expect any problems caused by groups 1+2+3, but as group 3 expands,
or groups 4, 5, and 6 appear, I would definitely expect there to be trouble
with ignoring grouping.

>I think people with large collections might be quitting because WW has
>told them they can't use their old cards with the new cards. Their
>motivation for buying new cards is gone, and for some people the game
>stops being fun when they stop getting new cards.

Hm. I'm pretty sure I can use all the new CE library cards with my old
crypt, and all my old cards with my new crypt. I can't use a small proportion
of my old cards simultaneously with a small proportion of my new cards.

That's not a huge restriction for me.

>> Currently there's about 15 vamps per clan per group.
>> That's exactly where it should stay. If any group goes
>> substantially over this the game is in serious trouble.
>
>Why? What kind of trouble would that create?

- Too much cross-clan overlap leading to easily made bizarro discipline
combos

or

- Too many useful mid-caps with in-clan superiors, making crypt selection
for, say, a canonical ANI/FOR/CHI ravnos deck trivial

or

- Too many weenies, making mono-<foo> trivial

Some of these problems were (are?) already extant, to hear some players
tell it.

gomi

I never said I had a better answer. I was merely pointing out that
claiming the current answer is the BEST answer is a bit foolish
without the presence of other answers to compare it to.

Personally, I would have reprinted the majority of the old Jyhad, Dark
Sovereigns, and Ancient Hearts vampires, and possibly some of the
unreprinted Sabbat vampires as well. That would solve the problem of
new players not being able to get their hands on the old vampires.

For players wanting new vampires, I would have "updated" some of the
vampires, especially the old Jyhad ones of dubious worth, with more
disciplines or new specials. If the old vampire was really bad, the
capacity could stay the same, and the new scheme could be applied. If
the old vampire wasn't bad, the new version could have a higher
capacity. Then instead of grouping, a new rule that said the new
versions of vampires did not replace the old ones, but still contested
them, could be created. The effect would be to get a new version of,
say, Raven, but one that could NOT be played at the same time as the
old Raven, because they would contest each other. The options would be
increased, because you could play either version of the vampire, but
you could still mix and match vampires from all editions of the game.

But that's just off the top of my head. It seems to me that with
serious thought, several alternatives that are at least as good as, if
not better than, the grouping rule could be created. Thus, it also
seems likely that the grouping rule is not necessarily the best
possible answer.

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Karol Magda wrote:
>
> <most of the post snip-ed, will adress only thing about library
> grouping>
>
> > And grouping vampires doesn't solve the analogous problem
> > > in terms of library cards, which to me, it seems like a more pernicious
> > > problem anyway.
> >
> > This is true, potentially. i think in the future, or past, it might be
> > necessary to group library cards.
>
> Definitely.
>
> Take MtG Type 1 for instance. Only like 5 cards from each new set are
> playable in that format. Slightly more are playable for Type 1.5 ,
> even more for Extended , like 10-15 percent of a new set is playable
> in Type 2 and lot of the cards are playable in Block Constructed

That's because the DCI has no concept of banning or errataing overpowered
cards unless they're *so* overpowered their effect simply can't be ignored.
Somewhat overpowered cards are ignored as a problem. Since the designers
of the early editions of Magic cards were so clueless about game balance,
many of the most overpowered as well as the worst examples of wallpaper
came from those printings. The result is that even after restricting and
banning the worst cards, it's still hard for the better balanced cards
printed in the last few years to make a dent in any environment that allows
old cards.

Also, the Magic designers don't seem to hold themselves to a very high
standard in terms of balance in general. So even in a single set even in
recent years, there's still far much variation in the value of various
cards.

> If you add 100 new cards to base of 2000+ cards the impact of the 100
> new cards is small unless you create power escalation curve. Which is
> BAD thing (and even Wizards are aware of this as seen in current sets,
> contrary to what many peoples seems to believe here)

True. And that point certainly does reduce the number of useful cards
recent additions are going to make effective in Types 1, 1.5, and 1.X.
But it's not the main thing. The main thing is that the variation in
card power is much less in recent years so players, preferring to use
the best cards available, will obviously choose to use the best cards from
old printings whenever possible because they're so much better.

> I would not like to see that happen in V:TES. (insignificance of new
> cards or power escalation) I am not saying it is happening now, it's
> might start to be a problem in distant (or not so distant) future.

V:tES is different from Magic in that the designers fix card balance
problems over time - even card balance problems that are somewhat
subtle. (In fact, I tend to think they've gone overboard at times with
the negative effect that unnecessary confusion is caused, but that's a
different subject.) For this reason, you don't have old cards hanging
around in the game that everybody loves because they're old mistakes and
they're just *better* than all the recent cards. Tomb of Ramses III,
Mind Rape, and Return to Innocence are examples of cards that the DCI
refused to fix when they were in charge of V:tES. Now they're fixed
and hence, no better than, say, Baltimore Purge more or less.

Over time, continuing to add more and more new cards should not cause
an issue of making the new ones insignificant. I do think card
_variation_ will get to be somewhat of a problem, as players with
particularly good, full card collections will be able to build better
decks by coming up with any possible combination of cards in existence.
It's hard to say how much of a problem that will be because we don't
have any previous experience to work with.

> The Block Constructed type of tournaments are considered to be:
>
> 1) most balanced of constructed formats
>
> -mainly because it's easier to catch possible broken combos in testing
> where only 500 cards exists in format compared to 2000+ cards format

That might be said of block vs. T2 but I've never noticed a significant
difference in how balanced block tournaments are vs. T2 tournaments.
Such a statement is absurd when comparing block tournaments to T1, T1.5,
and T1.X due to the existence of overpowered older cards that the DCI
won't ban or errata.

> 2) most popular of constructed formats (and yes Wizards do
> polls/researchs and DO care about their customers)

Again, not sure why it would be true of block tournaments vs. T2. But
balance is clearly a drawback in the other formats. Particularly
balance that emphasizes use of expensive, powerful old cards. At least
a power escalation curve would emphasize recent - and thus cheaper -
power cards. But, no, Wizards does these things in the dumbest ways.

> -because many cards otherwise not playable in other constructed
> formats are playable here (or biggest percentage of cards you buy are
> actually playable besides in draft)

All this amounts to is basically banning cards by card set that should
be banned or errated on an individual basis. You really can't draw any
conclusions from the experience of Magic. When unbalanced card problems
are actually dealt with correctly, I think you discover that *more* cards
get used and are considered playable over the course of printing more
cards. Not less.

> -new players can compete with old players

In a balanced environment, new players should be able to compete with old
players. It's clear players with large collections have an advantage
that starts out being quite substantial compared to a new player who's
just started collecting. However, as the latter gets hold of a certain
level in terms of variety of cards, the advantage is likely to become
fairly minimal. Again, the experience of Magic tells you nothing about
how this works in a game where problem cards are fixed.

> The extended format (where you can use cards from last 3-4 such
> cycles) is also very popular (although sometimes not very balanced)
>
> The problem is that even in extended cards phase out in T1 void.
> (because it becomes impossible to balance it)

(Sigh) It's not impossible to balance it. The DCI simply refuses to
do so.

> Grouping of vampires basically creates kind of 'block constructed'
> crypt but the catch is that no crypt 'cycle' phase out entirely (you
> can STILL play with group 1 vampires). It also enables to print new
> and interesting vampires which do have an impact (and think about how
> many of new CE vampires would not have an impact if grouping rule
> didn't existed)

But you could just print those cards without grouping. As I reject
your reasoning WRT using Magic as an example which explains why grouping
vampires is necessary, I likewise reject the necessity of grouping
vampires altogether. Curt Adams may document certain somewhat
significant effects of dial-a-crypt over the course of one base set to
two base sets plus several expansions of varying sizes. That's to be
expected since we're starting from a very small pool to one several
times its size. But I think it's reasonable to expect that factor to
level off over time. Grouping is really unnecessary to allow newer
players to compete.

> Grouping of library cards would open vast posibilities for new cards
> and abilities which do have an impact and are not broken (and it may
> become a problem otherwise in (not so) distant future)

It is unlikely to become a problem. At least, let it become a true
problem and then we can evaluate what to do about it. The MtG example
is not applicable to V:tES.

Fred

If you do not come with card variations within disciplines, the best
results would be as explained in 1)

If you variate the cards after some time every discipline would have

(and I am not criticizing designers here, actually I think they are

SW - was correction of what was wrong with Sabbat (lack of some
vampires, adding
new effects to new disciplines to help define them)

FN - repaired stupid DS/AH cards (and although boosters contained all
new cards

but it was
just it, repair)

prevent
stupid 'half my crypt are princes of different cities with all in
clans at superior' decks among other things (and yes as Derek, I too
think that mid caps would be even more problematic than weenies had no
grouping existed , having discipline advantage of old vampires and
action advantage of young vampires)

I like most are split discipline cards and multidiscipline cards ,
both of which exists in magic :) ('split' cards and multi coloured
cards)

Hovewer it seems to me that game cannot be pushed to altogether new
directions as it was in BL for eternity. So after some unspecified
time you would have to phase out cards in order to make room for a new
cards (by phasing out cards I mean grouping of library cards in this
context)

Except T1 every other format have banned list.

Actually I don't think Wizards are that dumb. There was one critical
point
in game (Combo Winter) but game is much more healthier now.

So what do you suggest ? Banning 100 most abusive cards in the game ?
Guess what ? Even after that another 100 most abusive cards appear.

The number of cards played in given format is some percentage of
number of cards in format. The greater the number of cards in format ,
the smaller the percentage.

playable in the
long run. I can't see why it is bad thing.

>

> players. It's clear players with large collections have an advantage

If there was no grouping of crypt my weenie animalism deck would be
much better than new players one ,because he would not have access to
Dani or Gillian Krader for example.

If many new animalism cards are printed with each new expansion, my
animalism
deck would be better for same reasoning. (since I would have acess to
ALL goodies , while he only to those from last expansions)

My deck would be more efficient both on crypt side and both on library
side. I would have GREAT advantage over him. EBAY is NOT an option for
most players.

> > The problem is that even in extended cards phase out in T1 void.

Worldgorger Dragon/Animate Dead combo is clear example that it is
impossible to balance vast formats while still printing new cards.
Note that
both cards are O.K. on their own. The only problem is that they exist
simultaneously in given format.

>
> > Grouping of vampires basically creates kind of 'block constructed'
> > crypt but the catch is that no crypt 'cycle' phase out entirely (you

> vampires altogether. Curt Adams may document certain somewhat
> significant effects of dial-a-crypt over the course of one base set to
> two base sets plus several expansions of varying sizes. That's to be
> expected since we're starting from a very small pool to one several
> times its size. But I think it's reasonable to expect that factor to
> level off over time. Grouping is really unnecessary to allow newer
> players to compete.

Magic and VTES have MANY things in common. Almost any given Magic
concept have
VTES equivalent and vice versa.

My group 1/2/3 Tremere would be WAY much stronger than new players
group 2/3 Tremere crypt wise.

It would be cheaper and filled with better vampires.

If you really want to see new cards printed for classic disciplines
(and not just card here, and card there among a dozens of reprints)
without giving too much advantage to old players (which WILL scare new
players from the game away, if they feel/think that they cannot
compete) then the grouping is one way to go.

Since it let old players to play with all his cards (although he won't
be able to mix some od them together) and it will allow new player to
compete (so he would not be scared off) it's quite reasonable solution
to both old and new players.

>
> > Grouping of library cards would open vast posibilities for new cards
> > and abilities which do have an impact and are not broken (and it may
> > become a problem otherwise in (not so) distant future)
>
> It is unlikely to become a problem. At least, let it become a true
> problem and then we can evaluate what to do about it. The MtG example
> is not applicable to V:tES.

I would rather identify a possible problem , analyze it and prevent
it. The let us destroy a world so we can built it anew attitude is
something I do not subscribe to.

Karol
